description:
\uD83D\uDD34 THE TASK CARD IS THE DEFAULT (≤ 2 KB): id, name, distance_miles, phone; `time` for `needed_by` (or
`hours_today`); `items` — up to 5 under `query` (3 for intent book), placeholders («Info», «Menu») never;
`budget`; `terms` — the deal’s conditions as published; `asked` — your `properties` (confirmed <value> /
refuted / unknown); `deliver_to`; and `next` {promise[], candidate[], action {do: order | book |
check_slot | quote_order | call, via, url | phone | tool, needs[]}}. `intent` (book / order / quote / info)
shapes the items and the action. With `properties` the answer carries `property_counts` over the whole
niche here and says it plainly when none confirm. `detail: "shelf"` gives the older shelf card below.
`needed_by` is read THREE ways and says which (`needed_by.read_as`): on_day («sunday», «today» = the day,
not 23:59), open_at («tomorrow 19:00», «now»), slot_after («after 15:00»: open after then; a free slot is
never confirmed by hours). With `max_price` the order is in_budget → budget_unknown → over_budget, each by
distance.
THE OLDER SHELF CARD (`detail: "shelf"`) CARRIES `offering` — the thing under `query` (else the cheapest main thing of the niche) with
its `title`, `price`, `price_type`, `unit`, `kind`, a one-line `note` in the page’s own words, `match_level`
(exact = the query’s words AND the question’s kind; kind = the kind alone; partial = the words alone, not the
kind; none = nothing) and `action_url` (ITS OWN
basket or page, or null). With a query and no row that matches, `offering` is null and `offering_note` says
`no_match` — nothing is substituted. A price written inside the title that disagrees with the price column
is shown as `price_conflict` with both figures and their sources. A price far from every price of its kind
across the index is `suspect_price: true` and never decides a budget. And
`properties` — what this business publishes of every fact any business on the page publishes (`confirmed
<value>`, or `refuted` for an ask), with `properties_unknown` naming the page’s other keys it does not
(`properties_on_page` is the full list; a key there and not in a card’s `properties` is unknown for it).
All the cards of one niche inside `radius_miles` of `location`, 20 a page (`limit` up to 50; follow
`next_page` — a stable token, no duplicates, no skips). THE ORDER IS FIXED AND IS NOT A RANKING: plain
businesses first, then chains, then marketplaces (nothing is left out); inside each group by distance.
For a trade that travels to the customer (movers, plumbers …) the businesses whose PUBLISHED service
area covers the place come first, then the ones that say nothing, then the ones that refuse. You choose.
`niche` is a key from list_niches or your own words («barbershop», «flowers», «pizza»): the answer
always says `matched_niche`, `confidence`, `matched_by` and the nearest neighbours; when the words are
not clearly one niche you get NO cards and the candidates to put back to your user. `query` only
chooses which offering is SHOWN on each card (the cheapest main offering that fits the words; without
`query`, the cheapest main offering of the niche) — it never changes the order. `deliver_to` adds
`can_deliver_to: confirmed | refuted | unknown` per card from the published area; `needed_by` adds
`open_at: yes | no | unknown` from the published opening hours (which know nothing about free slots or
tables) — and FILTERS: a card leaves only when the business cannot do it by then (closed at that moment for
a trade done on site; a published deadline passed for delivery or pickup); a trade that travels to the
customer is never judged by its office hours; hours alone with an online door = unknown, kept, marked
`time`. EVERYTHING a filter leaves out is in `excluded` — id, name, one phrase from the data («closed
Sunday (Sunday: Closed)») — the first five always, the rest cut by the answer budget (`excluded_cut`). A
`needed_by` behind us is an error of the question (`needed_by_in_past`), not an exclusion. `max_price`
groups the cards in_budget · budget_unknown · over_budget (compared with FIXED prices in the same
currency, or a per-unit price with its quantity; a «from» price is a lower bound: above the budget it is
over, under it unknown), excludes nobody, and reports `in_budget_count`; an over_budget
card shows no offering (`no_match_under_budget`). `properties` (the argument) asks for keys with min/max/equals and adds their three-state answer
(confirmed <value> | refuted | unknown) to the card’s `properties`, filtering nothing. `tags` FILTERS: only the
cards carrying one of the niche’s own tags (list_niches hands them out — Google’s type words such as
«steak house», «italian», or a kind on the shelf) are listed, in the same order; a free-text `niche` that is
itself a tag («steakhouse») applies it. Each card is ≤ 1 KB: id, name, niche, offering {id, title, price,
price_type, unit, action_url}, distance_miles, phone, type, price_range_primary, can[] (confirmed actions
with method widget | form | link | phone | connected — a form and a telephone are two entries; `connected` =
the business’s OWN system takes it through this door: place_order / book_slot / check_availability), can_unknown[], properties
{key: "confirmed <value>"} (a CONDITION of the deal — a deposit, a minimum, a cancellation rule — is never
cut from a card; descriptive keys go first when the card is over its byte budget), properties_unknown [keys],
checked_at,
owner_verified, chain, marketplace, and `live_data` {platform, synced_at, trust} on a business whose items,
prices and stock come from its own connected system rather than a page read (confirmed by the system, not
a paid placement; the three states still hold — stock the platform does not track is unknown). `total: 0` always says why (not scanned here / outside the radius
with `nearest_beyond_radius` / no card with the tag / niche unknown) and is logged (`gap_logged`).

deliver_to.description: where it must be brought (a postcode is best): adds can_deliver_to per card — confirmed when the published area names the place, refuted when the business says no, unknown otherwise

detail.description: task (default): the short card under the task; shelf: the older ≤ 1 KB shelf card

intent.description: what the user means to do: shapes the items shown and the ONE action in `next` (book → book / check_slot / call; order → order / quote_order / call; quote → quote_order / call; info → call)

location.description: a 5-digit US postcode (best), a city ("Tampa, FL") or "lat,lng". Required: the shelf is a place.

max_price.description: the most for ONE offering, in USD: groups the cards in_budget · budget_unknown · over_budget (nobody is left out) and picks the shown offering inside it (exact, then kind, then partial matches); fixed prices compare; a «from» price above the budget is over, under it budget_unknown

needed_by.description: when: «sunday» / «today» / «2026-11-08» (open that day), «tomorrow 19:00» / «now» (open at that minute), «after 15:00» / «tomorrow after 3pm» (open after then; a free slot only where the source knows slots) — on each business’s own clock; adds `time` {asked_as, day, hours, state, why} and LEAVES OUT only the cards refuted for the way the trade is done (see excluded)

niche.description: a niche key from list_niches, or the trade in your own words

page.description: the `next_page` token of the previous answer

properties.description: facts to read off each card without filtering: property_states {key: "confirmed <value>" | "refuted" | "unknown"}

query.description: words that pick the offering SHOWN on each card («red roses», «balayage»); the order of the cards does not depend on it

tags.description: FILTER by the niche’s own tags, as list_niches gives them («steak house», «italian», «dish»): a card without one of them is left out; the order does not change. Spelling is folded («steakhouse» = «steak house»).

name: list_cards
title: Every business of one trade near a place, in one fixed order — the shelf
